slides.title: Welcome and Calendar
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 2 English, Unit 1: Welcome and Calendar. You will learn how to say and spell your name, introduce a partner, and say what people like using like and likes. You will learn the calendar words too: the days of the week, the months of the year and the order words we use for dates. You will hunt for English words around your home, and ask simple questions about colours and numbers. By the end you will be ready to welcome a new friend, just as Amal does in this unit's story, “Amal's First Week”. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Say and spell your name, and ask others how to spell theirs.
Introduce yourself and a partner using simple sentences.
Say what you and other people like, using like and likes.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to say and spell your name, and ask others how to spell theirs. You will also introduce yourself and a partner using simple sentences. You will also say what you and other people like, using like and likes. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: train, snail, tail, sail, wait, week. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: A Poem: “When I Open Up a Book”
Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Words Around Us and A Poem: “When I Open Up a Book”. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: He and She: Choose the Pronoun
bullets: We use he and she so that we do not need to say a person's name again and again. Use he for a boy or a man, and she for a girl or a woman.
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is He and She: Choose the Pronoun. We use he and she so that we do not need to say a person's name again and again. Use he for a boy or a man, and she for a girl or a woman. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Introduce Yourself. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
